loci.textEn: Closes the sermon by reciting al-ʿAṣr: Allah's oath covers all humankind, saved only by the four traits.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 238 · Khuṭba fī qaṣr al-imāra bi-Kano

loci.textAr: ومن قال لكم قال الله تبارك وتعالى: ﴿اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم﴾ إلخ وهذا الورد جاء بعد هذا، فقولوا له: الورد مما جاء به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
loci.textEn: Answers the critics who cite the perfection of religion against the later wird: the wird is part of what the Prophet brought.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 240 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb

loci.textAr: وأنا أنصح من يشك في وجود الله تعالى ويشكك الناس فيه أن يشك في وجود نفسه قبل كل شيء. فالإنسان قبل أن يكون ما كان شيئا، ولما أراد الله إيجاده أوجده أطوارا وصفتها الآية: ﴿ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من سلالة من طين ... فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين﴾ وبعد بروزه كان طفلا صغيرا ثم صار شابا قويا ثم صار شيخا كبارا هرما
loci.textEn: Answers atheists by pointing them to their own stages of creation: let the doubter doubt his own existence first, then consider the Maker who brought him from nothing through these stages.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 242 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb

loci.textAr: وكل ما في هذه الدنيا من النعم فهو للمؤمن، وهو من بركة الإيمان، قال تعالى: ﴿قل من حرم زينة الله التي أخرج لعباده والطيبات من الرزق قل هي للذين آمنوا﴾ وإن شاركهم غيرهم في هذه النعم الدنيوية فلم يشاركهم فيها في الآخرة
loci.textEn: Reads the verse as making every worldly blessing belong to believers by the blessing of faith; unbelievers share them only in this world.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 242 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb

loci.textAr: فمعنى لا إله إلا الله عند العامة لا معبود بحق سوى الله، وعند السائرين إلى الله لا إله إلا أنت، وعند الواصلين لا إله إلا أنا. وهي مرتبة خاصة الخاصة. قرأنا في القرآن ﴿لا إله إلا هو﴾
loci.textEn: Grades the tahlīl: for the common people "no god but He" (third person), for travellers "but You", for those who have arrived "but I".
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 242 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb

loci.textAr: وقرأنا في القرآن ﴿لا إله إلا أنت﴾ ... فالغائب يشير إليه النحويون ب«هو» والحاضر يشيرون إليه ب«أنت» والمتكلم يشيرون إليه ب«أنا»
loci.textEn: Second-person grade of the tahlīl, for those travelling to Allah; maps the grammarians' absent, present and speaker onto three grades of realisation.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 242 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb

loci.textAr: وقرأنا في القرآن ﴿لا إله إلا أنا﴾ ... سمع موسى شجرة تتكلم تقول: ﴿إنني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا﴾ والشجرة ليست هي الله بل هي جماد لا تتكلم، ولكن الله القادر على كل شيء تكلم على لسانها ... هو الله القادر المتكلم بلسان آدمي ﴿أنا الله﴾ فإذا غاب العبد عن كل الموجودات وتجلى الحق فيه وصار لسانه الذي ينطق به
loci.textEn: Takes Allah speaking through the bush to Moses as the model for the "I" grade: when the servant passes away from all beings, Allah speaks "I am Allah" on a human tongue, as in the ḥadīth of nawāfil.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 243 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb

loci.textAr: وهذا غاية التوحيد، من وصل إلى هذا المقام برئ من الشرك تماما ... ومهما بقي شيء من الشرك بالله فثم حجاب بين العبد وربه، وما دام حجاب فثم عذاب. قال تعالى: ﴿كلا إنهم عن ربهم يومئذ لمحجوبون ثم إنهم لصالوا الجحيم﴾
loci.textEn: Reads the verse as making any residue of shirk a veil, and every veil a punishment: veiling precedes the Fire.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 244 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb

loci.textAr: وهذا الأكبر إذا وقفت بين يديه في الصلاة يأمرك أن تقرأ فتتساءل: ماذا أقرأ؟ فيقول لك قل: الحمد لله رب العالمين إلى آخرها ... وهذه مفخرة عظيمة أن يقول العبد ما قاله الله: الحمد لله ويعلم العبد حالا أن الرب سمع حمده
loci.textEn: Explains the Fātiḥa in prayer as Allah dictating to the servant what to say: the servant's "praise be to Allah" is Allah's own word, and "Allah hears who praises Him" answers it at once.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 245 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb

loci.textAr: «أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد» قال تعالى: ﴿إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر ولذكر الله أكبر﴾ الله تبارك وتعالى أمر بالصلاة في القرآن، وأمر بإقامتها وأدائها كاملة
loci.textEn: Heads a chain of verses on the prayer, close in sequence to the Kano palace sermon (p.224).
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 245 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb

loci.textAr: وأمر بالصلاة في الجماعة قال: ﴿واركعوا مع الراكعين﴾
loci.textEn: Congregational prayer commanded.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 245 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb

loci.textAr: وأمر بأدائها في الوقت فقال: ﴿إن الصلاة كانت على المؤمنين كتابا موقوتا﴾
loci.textEn: Prayer on time commanded.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 245 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb

loci.textAr: وأمر بالخشوع فيها وحضور القلب مع الله تبارك وتعالى، فقال تعالى: ﴿الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون﴾ فلا تكون الصلاة عبادة إلا إذا ربطت العبد بربه، وذلك لا يكون إلا بالخشوع والحضور
loci.textEn: Takes khushūʿ as presence of heart; without it the prayer does not bind the servant to his Lord and is not worship.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 245 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb

loci.textAr: قال تعالى: ﴿وأمر أهلك بالصلاة واصطبر عليها لا نسألك رزقا نحن نرزقك﴾ فهم العلماء من هذه الآيات أن من أتقن الصلاة وأمر عياله بإتقانها تكفل الله برزقه ورزق عياله من غير تكلف
loci.textEn: Reports the scholars' inference that Allah guarantees provision to whoever perfects the prayer and has his family do so.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 257 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb (section Hādhā wirdunā fa-l-yasmaʿ man yunkiruh)

loci.textAr: وردنا هذا: أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم. والله تبارك وتعالى يقول: ﴿فإذا قرأت القرآن فاستعذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم﴾ ونقرأ بعد ذلك فاتحة الكتاب
loci.textEn: Walks through the wird step by step, warranting each from the Qurʾān; first the taʿawwudh.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 257 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb (section Hādhā wirdunā fa-l-yasmaʿ man yunkiruh)

loci.textAr: والله تبارك وتعالى يقول: ﴿فاقرؤوا ما تيسر من القرآن﴾ وأفضل القرآن مطلقا فاتحة الكتاب. بدليل أنه لا يجب على المكلف من حفظ القرآن إلا الفاتحة
loci.textEn: Reciting the Fātiḥa in the wird obeys "recite what is easy"; the Fātiḥa is the best of the Qurʾān, being the only part every Muslim must memorise.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 257 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb (section Hādhā wirdunā fa-l-yasmaʿ man yunkiruh)

loci.textAr: بعد الفاتحة نقول: أستغفر الله مائة مرة. والله يقول: ﴿وأن استغفروا ربكم﴾
loci.textEn: Warrants the hundred istighfārs of the wird.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 257 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb (section Hādhā wirdunā fa-l-yasmaʿ man yunkiruh)

loci.textAr: وقال: ﴿فقلت استغفروا ربكم إنه كان غفارا يرسل السماء عليكم مدرارا ويمددكم بأموال وبنين ويجعل لكم جنات ويجعل لكم أنهارا﴾ هذه الأشياء كلا ببركة الاستغفار
loci.textEn: Draws from Noah's speech that rain, wealth, sons, gardens and rivers all come by the blessing of istighfār.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 257 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb (section Hādhā wirdunā fa-l-yasmaʿ man yunkiruh)

loci.textAr: مع أن التجانيين يفضلون صلاة الفاتح لما فيها من الفوائد. ونحن يكفينا فيها ما قاله الخالق الأجل: ﴿هو الذي يصلي عليكم وملائكته ليخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور﴾
loci.textEn: For prayer on the Prophet in the wird, cites Allah's own prayer on believers to bring them from darkness to light.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 259 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb

loci.textAr: والله تعالى يقول: ﴿ومن يعش عن ذكر الرحمن نقيض له شيطانا فهو له قرين﴾ فمن أعرض عن ذكر الله قيض الله له شيطانا هو إمامه حتى يأتي يوم القيامة
loci.textEn: Warns that whoever turns from dhikr gets a devil as his leader until the Day of Resurrection.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 259 · Majālis Kano: Tawsiʿat al-ʿilm wa-l-ʿirfān li-l-shuyūkh wa-l-shabāb

loci.textAr: ﴿حتى إذا جاءنا قال يا ليت بيني وبينك بعد المشرقين فبئس القرين﴾ ندم حيث لا ينفع الندم
loci.textEn: The neglecter of dhikr regrets his devil-companion when regret is useless.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 266 · Majālis Kano: al-Shabāb azimmat al-ghad

loci.textAr: فعلموا صبيانكم القرآن الكريم، فالقرآن إذا كان في صدر أحدكم علم العربية، وبالتالي لا يمكن لأحد أن يضله ﴿إن هذا القرآن يهدي للتي هي أقوم﴾
loci.textEn: Urges teaching children the Qurʾān so no one can lead them astray, since it guides to what is most upright.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 217 · Letter to General Catroux (Ḥaqībatuhu al-diblūmāsiyya)

loci.textAr: ولله على الناس حج البيت من استطاع إليه سبيلا
loci.textEn: He cites the hajj obligation to praise Catroux's provision of pilgrim passage.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 221 · Letter to the heads of al-Majlis al-aʿlā li-l-dīn al-ḥanīf, Senegal

loci.textAr: وكان حقا علينا نصر المؤمنين
loci.textEn: Promises Allah's help to a united Muslim party (Solidarité).
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 222 · Letter to the heads of al-Majlis al-aʿlā li-l-dīn al-ḥanīf, Senegal

loci.textAr: ولا تهنوا ولا تحزنوا وأنتم الأعلون إن كنتم مؤمنين
loci.textEn: Exhorts the leaders against weakness.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 222 · Letter to the heads of al-Majlis al-aʿlā li-l-dīn al-ḥanīf, Senegal

loci.textAr: وفي ذلك فليتنافس المتنافسون
loci.textEn: Urges competition in good works.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 222 · Letter to the mashāyikh al-Islām

loci.textAr: إن تنصروا الله ينصركم ويثبت أقدامكم
loci.textEn: Same argument.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 224 · Istiyāʾuhu min ḥarīq al-Masjid al-Aqṣā (1969)

loci.textAr: لا تجد قوما يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر يوادون من حاد الله ورسوله
loci.textEn: Warrants severing friendship/boycott of the aggressors.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 224 · Istiyāʾuhu min ḥarīq al-Masjid al-Aqṣā (1969)

loci.textAr: وسيعلم الذين ظلموا أي منقلب ينقلبون
loci.textEn: Threat to the wrongdoers.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 313 · al-Radd ʿalā man asāʾū al-fahm bi-shaʾn manẓūmat al-tawba (Yaqẓa wa-rudūd)

loci.textAr: قال تعالى في سورة النور: ﴿وتوبوا إلى الله جميعا أيه المؤمنون لعلكم تفلحون﴾
loci.textEn: Repentance is a commanded act of worship for all believers.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 313 · al-Radd ʿalā man asāʾū al-fahm bi-shaʾn manẓūmat al-tawba (Yaqẓa wa-rudūd)

loci.textAr: وقال في سورة التحريم: ﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا توبوا إلى الله توبة نصوحا﴾ فأنتم ... ترون أن الأمر بالتوبة يشمل المؤمنين جميعا، وأن تجدد المتاب إلى الله من مقتضيات الإيمان
loci.textEn: He reads the command as addressed to every believer, so renewing repentance belongs to faith and does not imply prior apostasy.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 314 · al-Radd ʿalā man asāʾū al-fahm bi-shaʾn manẓūmat al-tawba (Yaqẓa wa-rudūd)

loci.textAr: والإصرار على التوبة ... دليل السعادة وعنوان محبة الحق للعبد. قال تعالى: ﴿إن الله يحب التوابين ويحب المتطهرين﴾
loci.textEn: Persistent repentance signals Allah's love for the servant.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 314 · al-Radd ʿalā man asāʾū al-fahm bi-shaʾn manẓūmat al-tawba (Yaqẓa wa-rudūd)

loci.textAr: اقرؤوا هذه الآيات الكريمة من سورة غافر، وتأملوا أسلوبها الجميل الرقيق وكيف أن ملائكة الرحمن يدعون للتائبين
loci.textEn: The throne-bearing angels pray for the penitent.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 316 · al-Radd ʿalā man asāʾū al-fahm bi-shaʾn manẓūmat al-tawba (Yaqẓa wa-rudūd)

loci.textAr: [استغفاره ...] عن حضوره صلى الله عليه وسلم من حضور، قال تعالى: ﴿قل إن صلاتي ونسكي ومحياي ومماتي لله رب العالمين ...﴾
loci.textEn: The Prophet's repentance is a passage from one presence to a higher presence, since his whole life belongs to Allah.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

loci.textAr: من سنن الصلاة قراءة البسملة قبل أم القرآن في الصلوات كلها
loci.textEn: Opens the chapter on the basmala by stating that reciting it before the Fātiḥa is a sunna of prayer.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

loci.textAr: فالقائل بأنها آية من أول كل سورة يبسمل
loci.textEn: Draws the practical consequence: whoever holds the basmala a verse of every sūra recites it.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 196 · Letter to the Secretary-General of the Arab League (ʿAbd al-Khāliq Ḥassūna)

loci.textAr: ﴿اتقوا الله حق تقاته ولا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون واعتصموا بحبل الله جميعا ولا تفرقوا واذكروا نعمت الله عليكم إذ كنتم أعداء فألف بين قلوبكم فأصبحتم بنعمته إخوانا﴾
loci.textEn: Calls the Arab states to unity over Palestine with the command to hold fast to Allah's rope.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 197 · Letter to the Secretary-General of the Arab League (ʿAbd al-Khāliq Ḥassūna)

loci.textAr: فيها حق الأرحام ... ﴿واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا﴾
loci.textEn: Grounds Arab–Palestinian solidarity in the duty owed to kin.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 198 · Letter to Rābiṭat al-ʿĀlam al-Islāmī

loci.textAr: نجند أنفسنا لخدمة الدين دعاة إلى الخير كما أمر الله ﴿ولتكن منكم أمة يدعون إلى الخير﴾
loci.textEn: Commits the League's scholars to be the community that calls to good.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 198 · Letter to Rābiṭat al-ʿĀlam al-Islāmī

loci.textAr: ﴿كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس تأمرون بالمعروف وتنهون عن المنكر﴾ فبتلك الخصال وحدها لا بالدم والعنصر تكون الخيرية
loci.textEn: Explains that the umma's excellence lies in commanding good and forbidding evil, not in blood or race (ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām vs Abū Lahab; Salmān 'of the House').
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 199 · Letter to Rābiṭat al-ʿĀlam al-Islāmī

loci.textAr: والحكم الإسلامي عربي ﴿وكذلك أنزلناه حكما عربيا﴾
loci.textEn: Adds that Islamic law itself is 'an Arabic judgement'.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 200 · Letter to Rābiṭat al-ʿĀlam al-Islāmī

loci.textAr: ﴿لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف أو إصلاح بين الناس﴾
loci.textEn: Grounds the mediating role of the ʿulamāʾ.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 202 · Letter to the Secretary-General of the Arab League (second)

loci.textAr: فيها حق الأرحام وحق العقيدة حق الله ورسوله ﴿اتقوا الله حق تقاته﴾ الآية
loci.textEn: Grounds solidarity with Palestine in the right of faith.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 202 · Letter to the Secretary-General of the Arab League (second)

loci.textAr: ﴿واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام﴾
loci.textEn: Grounds solidarity in the right of kinship.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 202 · Letter to the Secretary-General of the Arab League (second)

loci.textAr: ﴿ولينصرن الله من ينصره﴾
loci.textEn: Second promise of divine help.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 204 · Letter on founding the Ittiḥād al-Ifrīqī li-Duʿāt al-Islām

loci.textAr: ﴿وقل اعملوا فسيرى الله عملكم ورسوله والمؤمنون﴾
loci.textEn: Urges work rather than politics.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 214 · Letter of congratulations to the President of the United States (Moon landing)

loci.textAr: ﴿ولقد كرمنا بني آدم وحملناهم في البر والبحر﴾
loci.textEn: Frames the Moon landing as Allah's honouring and carrying of humankind.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 214 · Letter of congratulations to the President of the United States (Moon landing)

loci.textAr: ﴿الرحمن علم القرآن خلق الإنسان﴾
loci.textEn: Attributes human knowledge to Allah's teaching.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 214 · Letter of congratulations to the President of the United States (Moon landing)

loci.textAr: ﴿وإن من شيء إلا عندنا خزائنه وما ننزله إلا بقدر معلوم﴾
loci.textEn: Science discloses treasures Allah releases in measure.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 214 · Letter of congratulations to the President of the United States (Moon landing)

loci.textAr: ﴿ويخلق ما لا تعلمون﴾
loci.textEn: New means of travel fall under what Allah creates 'that you do not know'.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 214 · Letter of congratulations to the President of the United States (Moon landing)

loci.textAr: ﴿والله خلقكم وما تعملون﴾
loci.textEn: Human achievement is Allah's creation.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

loci.textAr: أبدأ في الرد على تلك الفقرات بذكر شيء من آي الذكر الحكيم دستور الملة الإسلامية الذي ﴿لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه تنزيل من حكيم حميد﴾
loci.textEn: Announces he will answer the bishop with Qurʾānic verses, the 'constitution' of Islam.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

loci.textAr: ﴿قل اللهم مالك الملك تؤتي الملك من تشاء وتنزع الملك ممن تشاء ...﴾
loci.textEn: Argues that Allah gives and takes sovereignty, so colonial rule will pass.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

loci.textAr: ﴿إن الأرض لله يورثها من يشاء من عباده والعاقبة للمتقين﴾
loci.textEn: Same argument: Africa will be inherited by whom Allah wills.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

loci.textAr: ﴿ومن آياته الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر لا تسجدوا للشمس ولا للقمر واسجدوا لله الذي خلقهن﴾
loci.textEn: Asserts sole divine lordship against the bishop.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

loci.textAr: فهذا إعلان القرآن آخر كتاب جاء من عند الله ﴿إن الدين عند الله الإسلام﴾
loci.textEn: Calls the verse the Qurʾān's proclamation against Christian claims.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

loci.textAr: الطريقة الصوفية وعلى الأخص الطريقة التجانية التي نحن عليها طريقة النبي ... الذي يقول ﴿ادعوا إلى الله على بصيرة أنا ومن اتبعني﴾
loci.textEn: Identifies the Sufi and Tijānī path with the Prophet's own way of calling to Allah.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

loci.textAr: أمرنا في كتابه الحكيم فقال ﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وابتغوا إليه الوسيلة﴾ والوسائل إلى الله كثيرة وأكبرها هي التي جاءت في القرآن
loci.textEn: Reads 'seek the means to Him' as the Qurʾānic basis of the path and enumerates the means.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

loci.textAr: أولا اتباع النبي ... ﴿قل إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني يحببكم الله﴾ هذه الوسيلة توصل العبد إلى الله لأن محبة الله إذا حصلت للعبد وصل إلى حضرة الله
loci.textEn: First means: following the Prophet yields Allah's love, which brings the servant into the divine presence (with ḥadīth al-nawāfil).
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

loci.textAr: ثانيا ذكر الله في الغدو والآصال لقوله تعالى ﴿واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه﴾ علمنا بهذا أن مداومة ذكر الله آناء الليل وأطراف النهار وسيلة توصل العبد إلى حضرة الله
loci.textEn: Second means: the verse teaches that constant dhikr reaches the divine presence.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

loci.textAr: ثالثا مصاحبة شيخ عارف بالله قال تعالى ﴿واتبع سبيل من أناب إلي﴾ ومن أناب إلى الله في جميع حركاته وسكناته هو العارف بالله
loci.textEn: Third means: glosses 'the one who turns to Me' as the gnostic shaykh one must accompany.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 303 · al-Radd ʿalā ṣāḥib risālat Niamey

loci.textAr: تحديا سافرا ﴿فهل من مدكر﴾
loci.textEn: Closing admonition.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 305 · Nasf al-shukūk fī idkhāl al-mushrikīn al-masjid wa-ikrāmihim

loci.textAr: قلت والمشرك الكافر من العرب قال في تفسير الطبري ... والمشرك إذا سألته ما دينك فيقول مشرك لم يكن ليقوله إلا العرب
loci.textEn: Adds (qultu) via al-Ṭabarī that 'mushrik' properly names Arab idolaters, so European visitors are not meant.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 309 · Risālat al-tawba (al-Radd ʿalā man asāʾū al-fahm bi-shaʾn Manẓūmat al-tawba)

loci.textAr: وأن تعكفوا على القرآن الكريم تلاوة ومدارسة وتأملا ... ﴿إن هذا القرآن يهدي للتي هي أقوم ويبشر المؤمنين الذين يعملون الصالحات أن لهم أجرا كبيرا﴾
loci.textEn: Urges constant recitation, study and contemplation of the Qurʾān.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 310 · Risālat al-tawba (al-Radd ʿalā man asāʾū al-fahm bi-shaʾn Manẓūmat al-tawba)

loci.textAr: وقال ﴿واعتصموا بحبل الله جميعا ولا تفرقوا﴾
loci.textEn: Calls for unity.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 311 · Risālat al-tawba (al-Radd ʿalā man asāʾū al-fahm bi-shaʾn Manẓūmat al-tawba)

loci.textAr: وعمروا أوقاتكم بالصالحات ﴿سابقوا إلى مغفرة من ربكم﴾
loci.textEn: Urges filling time with good works.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 311 · Risālat al-tawba (al-Radd ʿalā man asāʾū al-fahm bi-shaʾn Manẓūmat al-tawba)

loci.textAr: ﴿وتواصوا بالحق وتواصوا بالصبر﴾
loci.textEn: Exhortation.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 7 · Khuṭbat al-jumʿa fī al-ḥathth ʿalā ṣalāt al-jumʿa

loci.textAr: وقد قال تعالى: ﴿يأيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا إِذَا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلَوةِ مِنْ يَّوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ فَاسْعَوا إِلَى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَذَرُوا الْبَيْعَ ... وَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾
loci.textEn: Cites the Friday verses as the command behind his exhortation to attend Friday prayer, followed by hadith on its merit.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 8 · Khuṭbat al-jumʿa fī al-ḥathth ʿalā ṣalāt al-jumʿa

loci.textAr: قال تعالى: ﴿إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انفَطَرَتْ وَإِذَا الْكَوَاكِبُ انتَثَرَتْ وَإِذَا الْبِحَارُ فُجِّرَتْ وَإِذَا الْقُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَّا قَدَّمَتْ وَأَخَّرَتْ﴾
loci.textEn: Closes the sermon with the eschatological verses to warn that each soul will know what it has done.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

loci.textAr: وتنافسوا في محبة حبيبه وصفوته، باتباعه وطاعته ... وقد قال تعالى: ﴿قُلْ إِن كُنتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي يُحْبِبْكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾
loci.textEn: Warrants his claim that love of the Prophet is shown by following him.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

loci.textAr: وقال تعالى: ﴿مَّنْ يُطِعِ الرَّسُولَ فَقَدْ أَطَاعَ اللَّهَ﴾
loci.textEn: Second verse in the chain proving that obeying the Prophet is obeying Allah.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

loci.textAr: وقال تعالى: ﴿وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ فَأُولئِكَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ النَّبِيِّينَ وَالصِّدِّيقِينَ وَالشُّهَدَاءِ وَالصَّالِحِينَ وَحَسُنَ أُولَئِكَ رَفِيقًا ذَلِكَ الْفَضْلُ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾
loci.textEn: Third verse: obedience to Allah and the Prophet brings the company of prophets and saints.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

loci.textAr: وقد قالوا إنَّ الإحسان يسترق الإنسان، والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هو المحسن إلى سائر الأكوان، مع ما فيه من أوصاف حميدة ... قال تعالى: ﴿لَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ مَا عَنِتُّمْ ... وَهُوَ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ﴾
loci.textEn: Cites the verses on the Prophet's compassion as proof that he is the benefactor of all beings and so owed love.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

loci.textAr: وقد قال تعالى: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ ... شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ الَّذِي أُنزِلَ فِيهِ الْقُرْءَانُ ... وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾
loci.textEn: Quotes the full fasting passage as the command behind the Ramaḍān sermon, then a string of hadith.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

loci.textAr: وقال تعالى - وهي آخر آية نزلت -: ﴿وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمًا تُرْجَعُونَ فِيهِ إِلَى اللَّهِ ثُمَّ تُوَفَّى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَّا كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾
loci.textEn: Closes with this verse, identifying it as the last verse revealed.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

address.raw: p. 14 · al-Khuṭba al-thāniya al-dāʾima li-kull jumʿa

loci.textAr: أمرنا أمرا بدأ فيه بنفسه، وثنى بملائكة قدسه، وثلث بالمؤمنين من جنّه وإنسه، وقال تشريفا لنبيه وتكريما: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَمَلَائِكَتَهُ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى النَّبِيءِ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا صَلُّوا عَلَيْهِ وَسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيمًا﴾
loci.textEn: Reads the verse's order (Allah, then angels, then believers) as a command Allah began with Himself, to honour the Prophet, and urges abundant blessing.
loci.editorialNote: The English is a summary of how he uses the verse here, not a translation of the passage.

Macaronic: the Wolof 'gerte' (groundnut) set in an Arabic hemistich. On whether zakāt is due on peanut crops; cf. ALA #18 Irshād al-sārīn ilā ʿadam al-hārīn, 1355/1936. Simultaneously poetic and juristic. VERSE IS INFERRED FROM THE SUBJECT, not named by ALA — the only entry here that is not ALA's own attribution.

The bāʾ of the basmala: the dot beneath the alif, tawāḍuʿ and rafʿ — man tawāḍaʿa rafaʿahu llāh. Hadith: mā bayna bismillāh al-raḥmān al-raḥīm wa-bayna al-ism al-aʿẓam illā kamā bayna sawād al-ʿayn wa-bayāḍihā.
alastu bi-rabbikum qālū balā — cited within the basmala discussion, on primordial speech.
[VERSE INFERRED FROM CONTEXT, no explicit lemma — check against source] The rivers of Paradise, named only as 'the verse in Sūrat al-Qitāl'.

Aqsām al-ḥamd; rabb al-ʿālamīn — al-ʿālam is everything other than Allah; the masculine plural by taghlīb. al-Rabb is the one who rears, whether by small favours or by great ones — ʿulūm, maʿārif, laṭāʾif, asrār.
al-Raḥīm: raḥma as riqqat al-qalb is impossible of Allah; its terminus, tafaḍḍul, is not. Hadith of the hundred mercies.
mālik yawm al-dīn — kings of this world are contested; He is not.

Taqdīm al-mafʿūl li-l-ḥaṣr. THE KEY DIVISION: iyyāka naʿbudu = sharīʿa, wa-iyyāka nastaʿīnu = ḥaqīqa. Then ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib on riyāʾ — ṣallaytu al-bāriḥa miʾat rakʿa. Collate against Fī Riyāḍ Lesson 1.

Allah did not say ṣirāṭ alladhīna qutilū wa-dhubiḥū. The objection from the four caliphs, all martyred though all prayed for ʿāfiya. Resolution: al-ʿāfiya huwa al-riḍā bi-l-qadar — not that the Master assist you in all you desire, but that you consent to every decree. al-maghḍūb ʿalayhim = the Jews, al-ḍāllīn = the Christians. NOTE the parallel four-caliphs excursus in Fī Riyāḍ vol. 1, pp. 56-59, on Q 2:3 (Wright 2024).

al-Raḥmān ʿalā l-ʿarsh istawā — inna l-ʿarsh maqlūb sharʿ: the consonants of ʿ-r-sh reversed give sh-r-ʿ. The Throne is where Allah's mercy descends, so the Law is the sum and landing-place of mercy on earth. NO PARALLEL FOUND in the published scholarship on Shaykh Ibrāhīm.

[VERSE INFERRED FROM CONTEXT, no explicit lemma — check against source] Jacob's letter to the king of Egypt; Joseph freeing the people of Egypt for joy at meeting his father.

hiya ʿaṣāya — al-ʿaṣā and al-maʿṣiya are cognate in the lafẓ: what the servant ascribes to himself becomes a living thing against him. Then Moses' tongue, the coal, and why the miracle required the earlier defect.
law kāna fīhimā ālihatun illā llāhu la-fasadatā — ʿilm al-kalām is blamed and an innovation, and this one verse suffices a man, on tawḥīd al-afʿāl wa-l-ṣifāt wa-l-dhāt.
wa-jaʿalnā min al-māʾ kulla shayʾin ḥayy — as water is the cause of every living thing here, lā ilāha illā llāh is the cause of life hereafter; that word is the water of the next world.

Taṣrīḥ against taʿrīḍ in supplication: Zachariah asks explicitly (rabbi hab lī min ladunka waliyyan) because he seeks a good; Job alludes (annī massaniya l-ḍurr) because he seeks the lifting of an affliction, and allusion is nearer to adab.

wa-lā tulhikum amwālukum wa-lā awlādukum ʿan dhikri llāh — whoever is not connected to the Presence is, ʿinda ahl al-ḥaqīqa, ibn zinan. Also the four gazes that count as worship: the Kaʿba, a parent's face, the muṣḥaf, a scholar's face.

FOUR LIGHTS: that which shows you and is not seen; that which shows you and is seen (the eye's light); that which only shows you (the intellect's light); and that which shows you the existent AND the non-existent — and that is Allah. Then the zujāja as the believer's heart: glass breaks fast; too much sleep, food and mixing with worldly people clouds it. COLLATION TARGET — Wright 2024 cites Fī Riyāḍ vol. 4, pp. 217-218 on this verse but does not analyse it.
man yamshī ʿalā baṭnih = appetite of the belly; on two feet = appetite of sex; on four = those who seek jāh, called four because they are ridden. And some of the ʿārifūn walk by their spirits.

li-yaghfira laka llāhu — the agent is not repeated; Allah assigns the act to Himself. The Prophet being maʿṣūm, the maghfira returns to the umma (cf. li-yudkhila l-muʾminīn). Three things no veil stops: a parent's prayer for a child, the prayer of the wronged, the word of ikhlāṣ.
wa-mā ṣabruka illā bi-llāh; wa-mā l-naṣru illā min ʿind Allāh; in yanṣurkumu llāhu fa-lā ghāliba lakum. 'Nowhere in the Qurʾān is victory mentioned without Allah being made its agent.'

alḥaqnā bihim dhurriyyatahum — the murīd of deficient state is joined to his shaykh's station as the child of deficient faith is joined to the parent's. al-marʾ maʿa man aḥabb.
kulla yawmin huwa fī shaʾn — the boy who answered from the floor and was raised to the minbar; he was Mālik b. Anas.
laʿib / lahw / zīna / tafākhur / takāthur mapped onto the seven-year ages of a life. Whoever has not repented to Allah by thirty is al-maghbūn.
fīhi baʾsun shadīdun wa-manāfiʿu li-l-nās — what is of general benefit Allah made cheap (iron, fresh water, air); what has no use He made dear (gold, musk). 'Thus Allah exchanged, out of His mercy.'
kallā innahum ʿan rabbihim yawmaʾidhin la-maḥjūbūn — the veil is the CAUSE of the punishment, as a sultan first screens himself from the man he means to punish.

yā ayyatuhā l-nafsu l-muṭmaʾinna — lā yumkin li-l-nafs al-iṭmiʾnān illā bi-l-maʿrifa. The souls of worldly people never rest: desire in pursuit cannot rest, desire in possession fears loss. WRIGHT'S 2024 THESIS (maʿrifa bi-llāh as the telos of Shaykh Ibrāhīm's exegesis) stated flatly in 1956, on a verse he does not treat, in a text he does not know.

aḥad indefinite because His unicity is hidden from creation save from ahl al-maʿrifa; al-Ṣamad definite because known even to the deniers (Q 29:61). lam yalid wa-lam yūlad negates being begotten BEFORE begetting, since the deniers claimed the latter and none claimed the former (Q 9:30; the Arab pagans on the angels). Then: aḥad is the trustee (amīn) the intellect seeks, al-Ṣamad the rich man (ghanī muthrī) desire seeks.
Cited within the al-Ikhlāṣ commentary.

qul aʿūdhu bi-rabb al-falaq — ONE name only (al-Rabb), because refuge is sought from four worldly harms and the need is worldly. ʿālam al-khalq (dense bodies) against ʿālam al-amr (luminous spirits, angels), from which no harm issues at all.

THREE names — rabb, malik, ilāh — because the need is religious. al-Rabb for the small, who need tarbiya and iṣlāḥ; al-Malik for the young, whose strength must be curbed by a king they cannot resist; al-Ilāh for the old, who have nothing left but return. Fa-l-nās thalāthat aqsām.

He quotes only as far as "min amr rabbī" and stops there, leaving out the rest of the verse. The citation is not exegesis of the verse: it licenses the taxonomy that follows rather than construing "amr". But the fatwā answers the question the verse itself records being put to the Prophet, so reading it as a bare proof-text understates what he is doing. occasions.label: The Kosi tafsīr, delivered without a book
occasions.note: Refused the loan of a Jalālayn by his brother Muḥammad Khalīfa, he delivered the tafsīr from memory. Seesemann p. 64 records the episode but warns the chronology of these early events cannot be fixed precisely (n. 62); the rupture with his brother came later, in 1349/1930-31 (p. 63). Dating soft; significance not.

occasions.label: The abbreviated answers, written at Kaolack
occasions.note: Signed in the printing: 'written in haste by the most ignorant of Allah's creation, Ibrāhīm b. al-Ḥājj ʿAbd Allāh al-Tijānī, at Kaws, the year 1349, two nights remaining of the Prophetic Rabīʿ.' The earliest dated locus in the corpus, and it falls in the fayḍa years — Seesemann places the declaration around 1929-30 and the rupture with his brother in 1349/1930-31. Shaykh Ibrāhīm opens by saying he is abbreviating deliberately, 'out of fear for myself of making the secret free for the taking', and then sets out the quṭb doctrine.
